suggestions.name: Urea / Ammonium Sulfate (Chemical)
suggestions.why: Nitrogen drives vegetative growth and chlorophyll production; deficiency shows as yellowing of older leaves and stunted growth.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 40-60 kg/ha in split doses: 50% at sowing, 25% at tillering, 25% at flowering.
suggestions.expected_improvement: 15-25% increase in nitrogen index within one crop cycle.

suggestions.name: Vermicompost / Farmyard Manure (Organic)
suggestions.why: Slow-release organic nitrogen improves soil structure alongside nutrient supply.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 5-10 tonnes/ha, incorporated into topsoil 2-3 weeks before sowing.

suggestions.name: Green Manure (Dhaincha / Sunhemp)
suggestions.why: Leguminous green manure fixes atmospheric nitrogen via root nodules.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Grow for 45 days then plough back into the soil before flowering.

suggestions.name: Single Super Phosphate (Chemical)
suggestions.why: Phosphorus supports root development and flowering; deficiency causes poor root growth and delayed maturity.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 50-80 kg/ha as basal dose at sowing, placed near root zone.

suggestions.name: Bone Meal / Rock Phosphate (Organic)
suggestions.why: Slow-release phosphorus source, ideal for acidic soils.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 200-300 kg/ha mixed into soil before sowing.

suggestions.name: Muriate of Potash (Chemical)
suggestions.why: Potassium regulates water balance and disease resistance; deficiency causes leaf-edge scorching.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 40-60 kg/ha in split doses during vegetative and flowering stages.

suggestions.name: Wood Ash / Compost (Organic)
suggestions.why: Natural potassium source that also raises soil pH slightly.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 2-3 tonnes/ha of compost enriched with wood ash.

suggestions.name: Agricultural Lime
suggestions.why: Acidic soils lock up nutrients like P and Ca, reducing uptake efficiency.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 1-2 tonnes/ha of ground limestone, tilled into topsoil 3-4 weeks before sowing.

suggestions.name: Gypsum + Organic Matter
suggestions.why: Alkaline soils suffer from poor micronutrient (Fe, Zn, Mn) availability.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Apply 2-3 tonnes/ha gypsum along with well-decomposed compost.
suggestions.expected_improvement: Lowers pH by 0.3-0.7 units, improves micronutrient availability.

suggestions.name: Drip Irrigation / Mulching
suggestions.why: Water stress reduces nutrient transport and photosynthesis.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Install drip lines or apply 5-7 cm straw/plastic mulch to reduce evaporation.

suggestions.name: Improved Drainage / Raised Beds
suggestions.why: Waterlogging suffocates roots and promotes fungal disease.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Create drainage channels or raised beds to divert excess water.
suggestions.expected_improvement: Prevents root rot, restores aeration within days.

general_rotation.threshold: Fertility score trending down over 3+ cycles

suggestions.name: Crop Rotation with Legumes
suggestions.why: Continuous monoculture depletes specific nutrients; legumes replenish nitrogen naturally.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Rotate cereal crops with pulses (chickpea, lentil, mungbean) every alternate season.

micronutrient_deficiency.threshold: Visual chlorosis or historically low yield despite adequate NPK

suggestions.name: Zinc Sulfate / Chelated Micronutrient Spray
suggestions.why: Micronutrients are needed in small quantities but are critical for enzyme function and chlorophyll synthesis.
suggestions.how_to_apply: Foliar spray of 0.5% ZnSO4 solution at 15-day intervals during vegetative stage.
suggestions.expected_improvement: Visible greening within 1-2 weeks, yield improvement of 8-12%.
